prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a side impact at intersection in Sugar Land, Texas, and has whiplash. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1443; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement is for our claim file. Can you please state your full name for the record?

A: Sure. I'd prefer to keep my name off the recording, if that's all right. I'm the driver of the blue sedan that was involved in the collision.

Q: That works. Can you walk me through where you were when the accident happened?

A: I was heading east on the main road in Sugar Land, approaching the intersection with a traffic light. My light was green, and I was going about thirty-five miles an hour.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the impact?

A: Not until the last second. A pickup came through from the cross street on my right side. I hit the brakes, but there wasn't time to avoid it. It struck the driver's side of my car.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?

A: Yes, I was.

Q: Did the airbags deploy?

A: No, they didn't. The impact jolted me sideways against the door and then snapped me back into the seat.

Q: Did you feel any injuries right after the collision?

A: My neck felt stiff almost immediately, and by the next morning I had pain running into my shoulders and a headache at the base of my skull. I've been turning my whole upper body to check mirrors because my neck won't rotate well.

Q: Have you seen a doctor or received any treatment since?

A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic the same day, and I've been referred to a physical therapist. I'm scheduled for sessions twice a week for now.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: Only that I was following the rules of the road and I'm hoping this can be resolved quickly, since I'm still having trouble driving and sleeping.

Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.
